Matthew 25:6 — October 22, 1844

The Midnight Cry

“And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold,
the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.”

— Matthew 25:6 (KJV)

In the fall of 1844, hundreds of thousands of Americans awaited the second coming of Christ on October 22 — inspired by the prophecies of Daniel 8:14 and the prophetic charts that made the vision plain. The charts are the tables of Habakkuk 2:2. The cry still sounds. The Bridegroom is still coming.

Study the Midnight Cry Watch the Documentary
The First Angel's Message

Behold, the Bridegroom Cometh

The parable of the ten virgins foretold the Advent movement precisely. The midnight cry was the proclamation that Christ was coming — October 22, 1844. Not all were ready.

Matthew 25:1–6 (KJV)
“Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom. And five of them were wise, and five were foolish… And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.”
— Matthew 25:1–2, 6 — The Parable of the Ten Virgins

“Fear God, and give glory to him; for the hour of his judgment is come: and worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters.”

— Revelation 14:7 (KJV) — First Angel: The Hour of Judgment is Come
Revelation 14:8 (KJV)
“And there followed another angel, saying, Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.”
— Revelation 14:8 — Second Angel: Babylon is Fallen

The Second Angel’s message of Babylon’s fall was inseparably joined to the midnight cry of 1844. Charles Fitch preached “Come Out of Her, My People” in 1843. Babylon had fallen — all the Protestant churches that rejected the first angel’s message of the judgment hour were swept into spiritual darkness. The cry of Revelation 18:4 echoes still.

Habakkuk 2:2–3 (KJV)

Write the Vision — Make It Plain Upon Tables

The Lord commanded Habakkuk to write the vision on tables — so he that runneth may read it. The 1843 and 1850 prophetic charts are the divine fulfillment of that command.

Habakkuk 2:2–3 (KJV)

v.2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.

v.3 For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.”

The Tables = The Prophecy Charts. The word “tables” in Habakkuk 2:2 refers to large writing tablets — exactly what the 1843 and 1850 prophetic charts were. These massive illustrated charts were carried to every campmeeting, hung on canvas, and used to preach Daniel 8:14 to hundreds of thousands across America. They fulfilled Habakkuk’s command: the vision was written plain, so that “he that runneth may read it.”

October 22, 1844 — Present Day

The Tarrying Time — Waiting for the 144,000

Though it tarry, wait for it — Habakkuk 2:3. Since the great disappointment of 1844, God’s remnant people have kept the commandments and waited. The sealing is not yet complete.

October 22, 1844

The Great Disappointment

Christ did not appear visibly. But the prophecy was not in error — the sanctuary to be cleansed was in heaven, not on earth. The investigative judgment began in the Most Holy Place.

1844 — 1848

The Sabbath Truth Restored

Captain Joseph Bates published The Seventh-Day Sabbath: A Perpetual Sign (1846). The fourth commandment — the seal of the living God — was restored to the remnant church.

1849

A Seal of the Living God

Bates published his landmark tract showing that the 144,000 of Revelation 7 are those sealed with the Sabbath truth — the seal of God in their foreheads before the four winds are released.

Now — The End

The Sealing Is In Progress

The four angels hold the four winds. The sealing of the 144,000 continues. The third angel’s message calls God’s people out of Babylon. “Here is the patience of the saints.” — Rev. 14:12

144,000

Sealed from the Twelve Tribes

Revelation 7:4 — “And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.”

Rev. 14:1

Standing on Mount Zion

“And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.”

Rev. 14:12

Keeping the Commandments

“Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” The 144,000 are Sabbath keepers.

The Fourth Commandment — Exodus 20:8–11

The Seventh-Day Sabbath — From Creation Throughout Eternity

God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it at creation. He wrote it in stone with His own finger as the fourth commandment. Isaiah 66:22–23 reveals the Sabbath will be kept in the new earth — from one Sabbath to another, throughout eternity.

Friday
Preparation Day
“the sixth day” — Luke 23:54
Sundown to Sundown
The Sabbath begins at sundown Friday and ends at sundown Saturday
— Leviticus 23:32

The Seventh Day
“the sabbath of the LORD thy God”
  • God rested on the seventh day and sanctified it — Genesis 2:2–3
  • Written in stone by God’s own finger: “Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy” — Exodus 20:8
  • The sign between God and His people forever — Ezekiel 20:12, 20
  • Jesus kept the Sabbath as His custom — Luke 4:16
  • The disciples rested on the Sabbath after the crucifixion — Luke 23:56
  • Paul preached on the Sabbath — Acts 17:2; Acts 18:4
  • The new earth: “from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me” — Isaiah 66:23

The Midnight Cry — Full Movie

In the fall of 1844, hundreds of thousands of Americans were inspired by the teachings and predictions of Baptist preacher William Miller and feared that the world would be destroyed by fire as he predicted at the second coming of Christ on October 22, 1844. Narrated by Cliff Robertson, this program uses original documents, stunning location footage, rich contemporary drawings and paintings, expert commentary, and moving readings from writers of the time.
